entities.name: Sabinus of Canosa
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Saint Sabinus of Canosa, venerated as a saint in the Roman Catholic church, was bishop of Canosa di Puglia from 514. He played a crucial role in the Christianization of Italy during the Late Antiquity period.

Sabinus was born into a wealthy family and received a traditional pagan education. He later converted to Christianity and became a priest before being ordained as a bishop. His leadership and commitment to the faith helped establish Canosa as an important center for Christian worship and learning.

As bishop, Sabinus oversaw the construction of several churches and monasteries in the region, including the famous Cathedral of San Nicola in Bari. He also promoted education and the arts, attracting scholars and artists from across Italy.

Sabinus' legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a key role in shaping the Christian identity of the region and inspiring future generations of Italian saints and bishops.
